Subject: Post-demo notes: Axion latency/throughput profile and open questions

Hi team —

Quick recap from today's call with Axion (Sara + infra lead): they run a real-time product recommendations API that must return a single LLM inference per user interaction. Key signals:
- Peak QPS: ~4.5k sustained during flash sales, typical baseline 500–1k
- Target 95th percentile (end-to-end) for the app: 60ms; they want to allocate ~30–35ms for the LLM inference portion
- Very sensitive to 99th percentile spikes during concurrency bursts (flash events)

Open engineering questions Sara asked us to clarify:
1) Can Redwood Hosted meet a 30–35ms inference budget at 4.5k peak QPS without observable tail-jitter?
2) What are tradeoffs (cost / cold-start / tail latency) vs a Dedicated pool?
3) If Dedicated is recommended, what pilot size / warmup cadence do we run to validate tail behavior?

I've attached the QPS sample file Sara promised — will help sizing. Next steps from the demo: one-pager with recommended pilot configuration + a short SLI checklist for their app team.

Ben — thanks for the recap. A couple clarifications from our infra side:

Sara — thanks for the detail and the artifacts. Short answer up front: for Axion's constrained per-request budget (30–35ms) at sustained 4.5k QPS with short bursts to 6.5k, we recommend a Dedicated pilot configured for predictable tail behavior. Hosted can be competitive for median/steady workloads, but two risk areas for Hosted in this profile are (1) tail latency under concurrent bursts and (2) transient cold-starts during scale events.

Rationale (summary):
- Tail variance: Dedicated pools allow tighter isolation and warmed KV caches per-tenant which directly reduces 99th/99.9th percentile token-step variance.
- Batching tradeoffs: To hit cost targets on Hosted you'd rely on aggressive batching which raises service-level variance during bursty traffic — risky for a 30–35ms budget.
- Warmup/warm cache: Dedicated lets us keep a reserved warm working set and use prewarmed burst nodes during flash sales.

Recommended pilot (2–3 weeks):
- Pilot size: start with 8 x A100-equivalent concurrent workers (we'll supply a recommended mapping to your QPS sample), configured with per-request concurrency limits and a reserved KV cache for hot prefixes.
- Canary routing: 5–10% traffic ingress to pilot initially, ramp to 30–40% given stable P95/P99 target.
- Observability: we will ship an SLI dashboard (token latency, model step latency, cache hit rate) and synthetic load harness to reproduce flash patterns.
- Rollback: Immediate fallback to Hosted variant by routing policy if P99 exceeds agreed threshold.

Action items I can take this week:
- Deliver a one-page pilot configuration + estimated committed cost (pdf)
- Provide sizing mapping (GPUs / concurrency per node) from your CSV
- Draft a short SLI acceptance checklist for your infra team to sign off

Can we schedule a 30-min call on Thurs 9/9 to review the pilot doc and confirm region mapping? I'll include Lauren to coordinate GA/infrastructure support.

Best,
Mina Haddad
